- Uncovered claim 'Expansion opportunities were slower to close than projected.' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim is specifically about EXPANSION opportunities being slower to close, but cycle_length_trend measures the average cycle length trend across all deals with no segmentation by deal type. There is no criterion that isolates expansion opportunities' cycle length, so a false claim (e.g., expansion deals closing faster than projected) would pass. The existing cycle_length_trend check CAN express this claim's substance but the drafted criteria do not segment by expansion vs. other deal types. (consider check: cycle_length_trend)

- Uncovered claim 'Committed pipeline overshot reality.' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim concerns committed PIPELINE overshooting actuals, which is a distinct concept from the overall forecast-vs-actual gap measured by forecast_vs_actual. There is no criterion that isolates the committed segment of the forecast. The existing forecast_vs_actual check CAN express overselling but the drafted AC1 uses target_pct 109 (a 9% overshoot) which matches the Q4 aggregate claim, not the committed-pipeline-specific claim. No criterion measures the committed-segment overshoot in isolation. (consider check: forecast_vs_actual)

The claim's substance is expansion-specific, so the existing check as drafted does not measure the claim's substance. No other check isolates expansion deal-cycle length. [note] Uncovered claim 'The gap between what was called and what closed widened through the back half of the year.' The drafted criteria never apply slippage_trend (AC1/AC2 use forecast_vs_actual against a single Q4 target, which cannot capture a trend across the back half). The claim's substance is a temporal widening, which slippage_trend can express but the drafted criteria do not. (consider check: slippage_trend)

AC1 and AC2 both use forecast_vs_actual, which measures forecast vs actual, not commit vs actual. No drafted criterion measures the commit bucket against realized revenue, so a dataset where the commit was roughly accurate (but the forecast overshot) would pass all criteria while falsifying this claim. forecast_vs_actual is the existing check that can express a commit-vs-actual overshoot; a commit_vs_actual-style criterion is missing.
